topic: keyless-sheets-auth: calling the Google Sheets API from a Node server (Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare / self-hosted) without a service-account JSON key, via Workload Identity Federation (host OIDC token) or a stored user OAuth refresh token, and what google-auth-library 11 requires for each

findings.claim: google-auth-library latest is 11.0.2 (published 2026-08-12). v11.0.0 (2026-07-29) has exactly one breaking change: minimum Node.js 22. The package now lives in the googleapis/google-cloud-node monorepo (core/packages/google-auth-library-nodejs); the old standalone repo was archived 2025-11-20, so its GitHub releases page stops at 10.5.0.
findings.evidence: npm registry: version 11.0.2, engines node >=22, repository directory core/packages/google-auth-library-nodejs; monorepo CHANGELOG: '## 11.0.0 (2026-07-29) BREAKING CHANGES: Update google-auth-library-nodejs to minimum Node version of 22 (#8995)'. googleapis 178.0.0 still depends on google-auth-library 10.5.0.

findings.claim: Service-account key creation is blocked by default in any Google Cloud organization created on or after May 3, 2024 (constraints/iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation and iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload are part of the enforced security baseline). The API error is 'FAILED_PRECONDITION: Key creation is not allowed on this service account.'
findings.evidence: 'Google Cloud security baseline constraints are enforced for all organizations created on or after May 3, 2024' listing constraints/iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation, constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload, iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts, iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, essentialcontacts.managed.allowedContactDomains, compute.managed.restrictProtocolForwardingCreationForTypes, storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess. Restricting-service-accounts page: 'If your organization was created on or after May 3, 2024, this constraint is enforced by default' and the FAILED_PRECONDITION error text.

findings.claim: Even where a key can be created, two policies can silently disable the site: iam.serviceAccountKeyExposureResponse defaults to DISABLE_KEY since June 16, 2024 (a key found leaked, e.g. in a public repo, is auto-disabled), and iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours (1h..2160h) makes newly created keys expire outright if an admin sets it.
findings.evidence: 'Starting on June 16, 2024, if you don't set a value for this constraint, Google Cloud will default to the behavior described for DISABLE_KEY' ... 'If Google Cloud detects an exposed key, it will automatically disable the key'; expiry: 'After this amount of time, the service account key expires, and you can no longer use it' (applies to newly created keys only).

findings.claim: The key-creation block can be lifted for one project by an Organization Policy Administrator (roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin) using 'Override parent's policy' on the project; the Workspace super admin who creates the organization automatically holds Organization Administrator and can grant that role. Changes take up to 15 minutes. So a key is not impossible, but it requires the owner (hello@serioludere.com) to act as GCP org admin.
findings.evidence: 'By default, the Google Workspace or Cloud Identity super administrator account that creates the organization resource is automatically assigned the Organization Administrator role.' Creating-managing-policies: select project -> Manage policy -> 'Override parent's policy' -> Add a rule -> Enforcement off -> Set policy; 'Changes to organization policies can take up to 15 minutes to be fully enforced.' Role: roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin.

findings.claim: Workload Identity Federation (WIF) works with any OIDC or SAML 2.0 identity provider and with X.509 client certificates; the Node library supports file-, URL-, executable- and X.509-certificate-sourced credentials plus a custom SubjectTokenSupplier. The credential JSON needs type 'external_account', audience '//iam.googleapis.com/projects/NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER', subject_token_type, token_url 'https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token', and (for impersonation) service_account_impersonation_url 'https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/EMAIL:generateAccessToken'. The federated principal needs roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on the service account.
findings.evidence: google-auth-library 11.0.2 README: 'a custom SubjectTokenSupplier implementation may be specified when creating an identity pool client ... Note that the client does not cache the returned subject token'; identitypoolclient.d.ts exposes 'subject_token_supplier?: SubjectTokenSupplier' with 'getSubjectToken: (context: ExternalAccountSupplierContext) => Promise<string>'; baseexternalclient.d.ts fields audience, subject_token_type, token_url, service_account_impersonation_url, scopes. Google doc: 'In Select a role, select the Workload Identity User role (roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser)'.

findings.claim: For Sheets, WIF must use service-account impersonation, not 'direct resource access': Google's direct-access list covers Google Cloud products governed by IAM, whereas a Drive file is authorised by sharing it with a Google identity (the service-account email). The impersonated SA needs no key; the sheet is simply shared with its email.
findings.evidence: WIF overview: 'most Google Cloud APIs support Workload Identity Federation, some APIs have limitations ... you can use service account impersonation'; the products-and-limitations page lists only Google Cloud services (e.g. 'Cloud Run doesn't support Workload Identity Federation direct resource access. To allow access, use service account impersonation') and never mentions Drive/Sheets; Workspace credentials guide: 'you can directly share individual files with the service account's email address using the standard UI'. Inference: a principal://iam.googleapis.com/... identity cannot be a Drive collaborator.

findings.claim: Vercel is the only one of the four candidate hosts with a host-issued OIDC identity. Vercel OIDC federation is available on every plan (Hobby included), must be enabled per project (Settings > Security > 'Secure backend access with OIDC federation', issuer mode Team = https://oidc.vercel.com/TEAM_SLUG), and Vercel's GCP guide gives a google-auth-library ExternalAccountClient example using subject_token_supplier { getSubjectToken: getVercelOidcToken }.
findings.evidence: 'OIDC federation is available on every Vercel plan, so no upgrade is required.' GCP guide: provider issuer 'https://oidc.vercel.com/[TEAM_SLUG]', map google.subject = assertion.sub, principal 'principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/012345678901/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/vercel/subject/owner:acme:project:my-project:environment:production', code uses subject_token_type 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt' and service_account_impersonation_url.

findings.claim: On Vercel the OIDC token is only available per request: inside functions it arrives as the 'x-vercel-oidc-token' request header (reused for up to 90 minutes, TTL 2 hours; build tokens 1 hour; development tokens 12 hours via 'vercel env pull' -> VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN). It cannot be read at module level. @vercel/oidc 3.8.5 getVercelOidcToken() reads globalThis[Symbol.for('@vercel/request-context')].get().headers['x-vercel-oidc-token'] and falls back to process.env.VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN. For Astro, the safest SubjectTokenSupplier reads the header from the current Astro Request (or from that symbol) rather than caching a token.
findings.evidence: 'Vercel does not generate a fresh OIDC token for each execution. It reuses a token for up to 90 minutes. Function tokens have a Time to Live (TTL) of two hours.' 'In the Vercel function environments, you cannot execute the getVercelOidcToken() function directly at the module level because the token is only available in the Request object as the x-vercel-oidc-token header.' Source get-vercel-oidc-token-sync.ts: getContext().headers?.['x-vercel-oidc-token'] ?? process.env.VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN; get-context.ts uses Symbol.for('@vercel/request-context').

findings.claim: Vercel's GCP guide tells you to paste the pool principal into the 'Service account users role' field, while Google's WIF documentation requires roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser for impersonation. Grant roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser explicitly (gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding) so the STS-to-generateAccessToken step is authorised regardless of what the console field maps to.
findings.evidence: Vercel: 'Paste in the IAM Principal ... in the Service account users role field.' Google: 'To grant the Workload Identity User role (roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser) to a federated principal or principal set, run the following command.'

findings.claim: Netlify Functions have no host-issued OIDC/workload identity token: Netlify's docs on 'identity' and JWTs concern end-user auth (Netlify Identity, deprecated) and the only documented Netlify-to-GCP pattern stores a service-account private key in env vars. Cloudflare Workers likewise have no native OIDC identity token (it exists only as a community feature request). Self-hosted Node has no host identity at all. On these hosts WIF is only possible with X.509 certificate credentials (self-managed CA) — supported by the Node README, but Google's page lists only Go/Python/gcloud.
findings.evidence: Netlify docs search returned only Identity/JWT/RBAC pages; dferber.de (2019) stores GCP_CLIENT_EMAIL/GCP_PRIVATE_KEY; Cloudflare community thread 'JWT OIDC Token in Workers - Feature Request'. X.509: 'Create self-signed certificates' supported, 'Number of trust anchors: 3', client libs listed: Go cloud.google.com/go/auth 0.16.0+, Python google-auth 2.39.0+, gcloud 538.0+; Node README has section 'X.509 certificate-sourced credentials' with --credential-cert-path flags.

findings.claim: A stored user OAuth refresh token is a host-agnostic keyless path. google-auth-library 11.0.2 exposes UserRefreshClient({clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken}) (type 'authorized_user') and GoogleAuth accepts credentials of that shape via fromJSON; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS may also point at an authorized_user JSON. The library auto-refreshes access tokens when a refresh_token is present; the refresh token is only returned on first authorisation, so request access_type=offline and prompt=consent once.
findings.evidence: refreshclient.d.ts: 'export declare const USER_REFRESH_ACCOUNT_TYPE = "authorized_user"; interface UserRefreshClientOptions extends OAuth2ClientOptions { clientId?, clientSecret?, refreshToken? }'; googleauth.d.ts: 'credentials?: JWTInput | ExternalAccountClientOptions | GdchCredentialsInput', 'JSONClient = JWT | UserRefreshClient | BaseExternalAccountClient | ...'. README: 'This library will automatically obtain an access_token, and automatically refresh the access_token if a refresh_token is present. The refresh_token is only returned on the first authorization'; 'ensure the call to generateAuthUrl sets the access_type to offline ... To force consent, set the prompt property to consent'.

findings.claim: Refresh-token durability: make the OAuth consent screen user type 'Internal' (project must sit in the owner's Google Cloud organisation). Internal apps skip verification, may use the sensitive 'spreadsheets' scope without review, and are not subject to the 7-day 'Testing' expiry that applies to External apps. Remaining revocation causes: user revokes, unused for six months, >100 live refresh tokens per account per client, Workspace admin sets the service to Restricted, or a password change when Gmail scopes are involved (not our case).
findings.evidence: 'Projects associated with a Google Cloud Organization can configure Internal users to limit authorization requests to members of the organization.' Testing (External): 'authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent' and offline tokens 'will also expire'. OAuth2 docs list: revoked, 'not been used for six months', password change with Gmail scopes, '100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID', admin Restricted services. Workspace guide: for internal apps 'use of restricted or sensitive scopes doesn't require further review by Google'.

findings.claim: Two further lifecycle rules for the refresh-token path: Google deletes OAuth clients that have made no token exchanges and had no config edits for 6 months (restorable for 30 days) — irrelevant while the site refreshes every hour, but fatal if the site is paused; and if the Workspace admin sets Drive/Sheets to 'Restricted' in API controls, an internal app must be marked trusted ('Trust internal apps') or its tokens are revoked.
findings.evidence: 'Google reserves the right to delete unused OAuth clients if the client is inactive for at least 6 months ... Deleted clients can be restored in the Google Cloud Console for 30 days following deletion.' Admin help: 'Only internal and third-party apps configured with a Trusted or Specific Google data access setting can access data' and 'If you change access to Restricted, any previously installed apps that you haven't trusted stop working, and tokens are revoked.'

findings.claim: Sheets API scopes: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets and spreadsheets.readonly are 'sensitive'; drive.file is non-sensitive (recommended by Google) but only covers files the app created or the user opened through it, so for an owner-authored sheet use 'spreadsheets' (fine for an Internal app or for an impersonated service account, where no consent screen applies).
findings.evidence: Scopes page classifies spreadsheets and spreadsheets.readonly as Sensitive, drive.file as Non-sensitive (Recommended: 'only the specific Google Drive files you use with this app'), drive and drive.readonly as Restricted.

findings.claim: Two more keyless options exist but are weaker fits: (a) an API key can read a spreadsheet only if it is shared 'Anyone on the Internet with this link' — read-only and the Votes tab would have to live in a separate private spreadsheet; (b) hosting on Google Cloud (Cloud Run etc.) gives the attached service account automatically through the metadata server (ADC search order step 3), no key or WIF at all — but that is outside the four listed hosts.
findings.evidence: API keys 'anonymously access publicly available data, such as Google Workspace files shared using the Anyone on the Internet with this link sharing setting'. ADC order: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS -> local ADC file -> 'Attached service account via metadata server'; Google calls keys 'the least secure option'.

findings.claim: Workaround to avoid the org policy entirely — create the GCP project under a personal Gmail account (no organisation, so no baseline constraints) and share the sheet with that project's service account — depends on the Workspace Drive setting 'Sharing outside of your organization' being On; if it is Off or Allowlisted-domains, the share is blocked. It also moves the credential outside the owner's control, so it is not recommended.
findings.evidence: Admin help: options 'On', 'Allowlisted Domains', 'Off'; when Off users cannot share 'Invitations to items created in Docs, Sheets, and Slides' and 'External users also lose access to any items previously shared with them.' Baseline constraints apply to organizations, not to no-org projects (secure-by-default page).

findings.claim: Client-library contradiction resolved for this gap: auth choice does not constrain the Sheets client. Both ExternalAccountClient and UserRefreshClient expose the same AuthClient.fetch()/getAccessToken() surface, google-spreadsheet 5.3.0 accepts any google-auth-library client, and the raw-fetch path in the sheets-api topic works unchanged. Caveat: googleapis 178.0.0 pins google-auth-library 10.5.0, so mixing an 11.x client into googleapis' typed constructors may produce TypeScript type mismatches; @googleapis/sheets 14.0.0 or authClient.fetch() avoids that.
findings.evidence: google-spreadsheet README: 'multiple auth options (via google-auth-library) - service account, OAuth, API key, ADC, etc'; npm: googleapis 178.0.0 dependencies include google-auth-library 10.5.0; google-auth-library README shows client.fetch(url) on JWT, ExternalAccountClient and OAuth2Client alike.

code_snippets.purpose: Vercel only: keyless Sheets client via Workload Identity Federation. One client per request; the SubjectTokenSupplier reads the per-request x-vercel-oidc-token header (falls back to VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN for `vercel env pull` local dev). Requires google-auth-library 11.0.2 (Node 22+).
gcloud one-time setup for the Vercel WIF pool, provider, keyless service account and the impersonation grant (then share the spreadsheet with the SA email in the Sheets UI).
code_snippets.code:
PROJECT_ID=serio-ludere-site; PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format='value(projectNumber)')
TEAM=your-vercel-team-slug; VPROJECT=serio-ludere

gcloud services enable sts.googleapis.com iamcredentials.googleapis.com sheets.googleapis.com --project=$PROJECT_ID

gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create vercel --location=global --display-name=Vercel --project=$PROJECT_ID

gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc vercel \
  --location=global --workload-identity-pool=vercel --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --issuer-uri="https://oidc.vercel.com/$TEAM" \
  --allowed-audiences="https://vercel.com/$TEAM" \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub" \
  --attribute-condition="assertion.sub=='owner:$TEAM:project:$VPROJECT:environment:production'"

gcloud iam service-accounts create sheets-site --display-name="Serio Ludere site (no key)" --project=$PROJECT_ID

# Google's WIF docs require roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser for impersonation
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding sheets-site@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID --role=roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser \
  --member="principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/$PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/vercel/subject/owner:$TEAM:project:$VPROJECT:environment:production"

# Vercel env vars: GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER, GCP_WIF_POOL_ID=vercel, GCP_WIF_PROVIDER_ID=vercel, GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL
# Then: Sheets UI -> Share -> sheets-site@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com (Editor if the site writes votes)

code_snippets.purpose: Host-agnostic (Netlify / Cloudflare-Node / self-hosted / Vercel): keyless Sheets auth with the owner's stored OAuth refresh token. Three env vars, no service-account key, no org-policy exception.

One-time local script to mint the refresh token for the owner (run once by the developer, owner signs in with hello@serioludere.com). Consent screen must be user type Internal; OAuth client type 'Web application' with redirect http://localhost:3000/oauth2callback.
code_snippets.source_url: google-auth-library 11.0.2 README, sections 'OAuth2' / 'Handling token events' / 'Retrieve access token' (npm tarball); https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration

recommendation:
1. Yes: the site can call the Sheets API with no service-account key on every candidate host, so the ADR must not depend on one (new GCP orgs block key creation by default, and DISABLE_KEY leak-response can kill a key silently).
2. Make the keyless path the default and rank by host: (a) Vercel -> Workload Identity Federation with ExternalAccountClient + subject_token_supplier reading x-vercel-oidc-token, impersonating a keyless service account that the sheet is shared with (zero stored secrets; roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser; all Vercel plans). (b) Netlify / Cloudflare-Node / self-hosted (no host identity) -> the owner's OAuth refresh token via UserRefreshClient with an Internal consent screen (no verification, no 7-day expiry); three env vars.
3. Ship the refresh-token path as the universal fallback even on Vercel (it is host-agnostic and needs only the GCP project to sit in the Workspace org); treat 'invalid_grant' as a monitored failure that serves the last-good cache and pages the owner to re-consent.
4. The Apps Script execute-as-owner web app stays the zero-credential baseline for votes if neither is set up on day one; it needs no key and no OAuth client.
5. Only if the owner refuses both: have them (as org admin) override iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation on the single project, and document the leak/expiry policies.
6. Pin google-auth-library ^11.0.2 (Node 22+); use authClient.fetch() or @googleapis/sheets 14 rather than googleapis 178 (still on auth-lib 10.5.0).
7. Keep the GCP project inside the owner's Workspace organisation (needed for 'Internal'); mark the app trusted in Admin > API controls if any service is Restricted.
open_questions: Does hello@serioludere.com's Workspace already have a Google Cloud organisation, and was it created on/after 2024-05-03? (Determines whether key creation is blocked; the org is auto-created when a Workspace user first creates a project/billing account.) Is hello@ the super admin?

Does Vercel's runtime populate globalThis[Symbol.for('@vercel/request-context')] for @astrojs/vercel functions so @vercel/oidc's getVercelOidcToken() works, or must the SubjectTokenSupplier read Astro.request.headers.get('x-vercel-oidc-token') as in the snippet? Not verified against an Astro deployment.

Sheets/Drive requiring service-account impersonation (no 'direct resource access' for Workspace files) is inferred from Google's product list and Drive sharing semantics; Google publishes no explicit sentence about Workspace APIs.

Absence of host-issued OIDC tokens on Netlify and Cloudflare Workers is established only by absence from their official docs as of 2026-09-05 plus a Cloudflare community feature request; a newer feature could exist unannounced.
Node support for X.509-certificate WIF is documented in the google-auth-library README but Google's feature page lists only Go, Python and gcloud; untested here.

Vercel's GCP guide grants the pool principal via the console's 'Service account users role' field; whether that alone suffices for generateAccessToken (vs roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser per Google docs) was not tested — the snippet grants workloadIdentityUser explicitly.

Whether the owner's Workspace tenant has Drive/Sheets set to 'Restricted' in API controls (would require marking the internal app trusted) and whether external Drive sharing is On (affects the no-org workaround).
TypeScript compatibility of passing a google-auth-library 11.x client into googleapis 178 (which depends on 10.5.0) was not verified.
